newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai to brief media on planned merger with Sega.
newsitem.headline: Bandai to brief media on planned merger with Sega.

text.p: Bandai Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it will hold a news conference on its planned merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd at 10 p.m. (1300 GMT).

Earlier, Jiji news agency reported that Sega will hold a news conference at 9 p.m. (1200 GMT) to announce the cancellation of the merger. Jiji also reported that the two firms are still planning a business tie-up.
A spokeswoman for Sega could not immediately confirm the Jiji report.
A Bandai spokeswoman declined to give further details.
On Monday, toy maker Bandai said it expected its board to approve at a meeting on May 28 a planned merger with Sega, withdrawing an earlier plan to postpone approval until July.
"Preparations for the merger are going forward steadily," Mikio Ishigami, a managing director of Bandai, told reporters at that time, adding that the planned merger date had not changed.
The company would try to remove any uncertainty among its workers about the planned merger, he added.
At the beginning of this year, Bandai and Sega announced that they would merge on October 1.
Japanese media reports have speculated that the merger could be delayed due to strong opposition from mid-level managers at Bandai.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Monday that Bandai's board in early May voted to delay approval of the merger until July, citing opposition within the company.
Bandai's business has recently been boosted by the huge popularity of its "Tamagotchi" electronic pet toy.
Japanese media also reported over the weekend that Bandai employees opposed the planned merger.
